```sql
WITH filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
lines AS (
    SELECT fo.id AS order_id,
           pv.product_id,
           pv.id AS variant_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM filtered_orders fo
      JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = fo.id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
),
per_order AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           order_id,
           sum(quantity)         AS qty,
           sum(line_total_cents) AS rev
      FROM lines
     GROUP BY product_id, order_id
),
per_product AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)                   AS order_count,
           sum(qty)::bigint           AS quantity,
           sum(rev)                   AS revenue_cents
      FROM per_order
     GROUP BY product_id
),
variant_counts AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM lines) dv
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       pp.order_count,
       pp.quantity,
       pp.revenue_cents,
       vc.variant_count
  FROM per_product pp
  JOIN variant_counts vc ON vc.product_id = pp.product_id
  JOIN products p        ON p.id = pp.product_id
 ORDER BY pp.quantity DESC, pp.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orderfilter wordt eerst en eenmalig toegepast, en de aggregaties gebeuren met hash-aggregaten in plaats van `count(DISTINCT ...)` op een grote sortering. Het `::bigint` op de quantity-som en de join met `products` pas aan het einde houden de kolomtypes en de rijvolgorde gelijk aan het origineel. Bij gelijke quantity- en omzetwaarden blijft de volgorde, zoals in het origineel, niet deterministisch.
